sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **A part named by its adjective alone is now recognised as a part.** The product-type rule reads what a title says the product *is* — its head noun — and skips the adjectives in front of it, so "Защитное стекло" and "Стекло защитное" both resolve to стекло. A shopper does not always write the noun: "защитное note 13 pro 4g" names the part by the adjective and leaves "стекло" unsaid. The query then carried no type the rule could match, so it stood down entirely and answered a request for a screen protector with flex cables, SIM trays and back covers — for the right phone, which is what made them look plausible. Measured on a 12 700-product parts shop, eight of the ten results were the wrong part. The adjectives in front of the noun are now kept beside it, and either can identify the part: the same query returns the two protectors and nothing else, the protector that actually lists that model first. Naming the noun still works exactly as before, and a query naming a different part still excludes the protectors.
